args.title: What an Attraction Layer anchor does when the far end dies
args.rule_text: An Attraction Layer bond does not tear when the far end dies. The seating holds for a short measurable interval after the body stops (one and a half seconds on the page), then the whole structure comes out of the Crystal in one piece and leaves the socket open. Lattice built around the seating collapses through the Shell in the order it was laid down, and the body pays at whatever points the preceding hours left weakest. The practitioner has every instant of the interval.
args.rationale: No rule row governs. R29-1-SACRAMENT_BOND_ANCHOR_BY_DECLARATION covers a different bond and says of itself 'this rule is silent on ending'. The Living System (Part Fourteen, no rule row) says Attraction Force bonds 'survive time, death, distance and change' and lists 'Carrying bonds past death in forms that remain clean and reciprocal', while the collapse the page describes matches its Obsession degradation ('removal of the object produces fracture events'). Which force the Sodoku-Hild bond ran under, and whether the page's mechanism is canon, is for Isaac; the rule text is the page's own account so he can adopt or strike it whole.

proposals.quote: An Attraction Layer bond does not tear. It is seated, and when the far end stops existing the seating has nothing to hold against, and the whole structure comes out of the Crystal in one piece and leaves the socket open.
proposals.why: The scene states a mechanism no pack states. Proposed as written on the page, not as a resolution of the Living System's two readings.

args.target: C-NEW (recalescence: converted grief, compound sentence, or chemistry)
args.note: Not yet a row. The scene's spine is a thermodynamic account of grief. R16-7-NOT_CONVERTED: 'It does not apply to: - The body. Chest, hands, gut. ... - Grief and the elegiac beat. ... A converted grief is a failed grief.' R16-3-COMPOUND_SENTENCE licenses '[the real phenomenon, correctly named] + [the system term as its name, its boundary condition, or its address] + [what the body or the room did]'. R6-2-CHEMISTRY_BAN bars 'Real-world scientific vocabulary explaining a sensory impression ... unless the POV is a practitioner of that specific craft actively diagnosing.' Sodoku is not a metallurgist. Whether the passage is a converted grief (fail), a compound technical sentence (pass) or ambient chemistry (fail) is not settled by the rules. Related: the R6-3-IGNORANCE_QUOTA candidate 'he had no framework for it' is rescued one section later by 'Recalescence.', and the Wellspring name in narration ('Oblation converts identity into intensity') sits on R9-2-VOCAB_BAN_NARROWED (Wellspring names banned absolutely) against R12-1-PACK_SEVEN_REPEALED and R13-9-STYLE_DIRECTIVE_MECHANISM_VOCAB's diagnostic-voice carve-out.

args.title: What a Gisei-surrendered memory leaves
args.rule_text: A memory surrendered to Gisei leaves a shape with no contents. The practitioner feels the conversion and does not feel what left; afterward he can find where the memory was and cannot know what it held. There is no recovery and no appeal.
args.rationale: The Asami and Gisei page (no rule row) says of memories: 'A specific memory, permanently surrendered. Not suppressed. Not forgotten in the recoverable sense. Erased from the Core's identity layer as though it never existed.' A findable shape may or may not be consistent with 'as though it never existed'. The page's residue is proposed for the Ledger (P04) and later scenes need to know whether Sodoku can notice the gap. Rule text is the page's own account, for Isaac to adopt or strike.

proposals.quote: He felt the conversion happen and did not feel what left. That is how it is built. The output arrived in his hands and the room went out of him at the same instant, and afterward there was a shape where the kitchen had been and no contents in the shape
proposals.why: A mechanism the page asserts and no rule row governs.

The one Front the page touches is the Tenrai, which is closed ('Kept for the record'): Seiji is alive eight miles up the road here and L004 has him dead a year on, which is not a contradiction. Two things on the page have a Front's shape and no Front: the strands and the brother in the Ashgate valley (P06, P13), and the man with Hild's circlet (P12). Both wants are unknown, so no add_front is drafted; Isaac decides whether either becomes one.

proposals.quote: Seiji Tenrai Moto was eight miles up that road with six hundred men and a claim and four sets of messengers on four corridors.
proposals.why: Table Rule 4 is not met by this session and the note says why rather than inventing a tick.

proposals.quote: Every Ice-out since, the ground opens and the whole winter's dead go in together and their names are read in the order they died, and what reads them now is a man with a list doing his best.
proposals.why: R6-9: 'Identity is repetition. Novelty is its enemy.' The recurrence FAIL and the new Kharven texture are one decision for Isaac.

args.note: The card's bond row reads 'Sonzai Moto (brother, separated) — Heavy, unresolved. The Kamigan's threat-queue on his whereabouts has never closed.' The page has Sodoku able to locate 'exactly' the point in the Ashgate valley the first strand went down to, knowing 'whose point it was' since the whistle, and calling that man his brother. The page never names him. If the brother is Sonzai, the card's open threat-queue on his whereabouts is contradicted; if not, the card is missing a brother.

args.note: Invented this scene as the PC's own figure and likely to recur: supercooling / recalescence (a soul held below the point, undischarged, waiting on a seed; the front running in dendrites along the avenues of the arms; the latent heat coming out as steam). If it recurs it is an Inventory item; if it is a one-scene figure R6-9 says it does not exist after tonight. Also new: the Tenrai as 'architecture' (the corridor design, the marriage south), which the page uses four times.

proposals.quote: The front started at the Soul Crystal and propagated outward and it did not travel evenly, it went in branches, dendrites, running out along the paths that were already there, and the paths that were already there were the avenues of his arms.

args.note: The unnamed killer in the corridor (the author notes call it 'Shiraku unnamed'; the page names nobody) is given three tells that should recur if it ever returns: a smell of damp stone, lamp oil and turned flowers; a second blade at the left hip in a scabbard two inches too short with the exposed steel gone dull grey; and shutting a wing by putting the shutting into the guards' heads instead of the doors. proposals.quote: It smelled of damp stone and lamp oil and something sweet under both, flowers left in a sealed room until they turned. It had a second blade at the left hip in a scabbard two inches too short, so the last of the steel stood exposed and had gone dull grey with it.
proposals.why: Three invented, recurrable details on an unnamed figure; the notes' name is not carried into the proposal.
